Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 32, English)
Humanity Over Power , the Real Definition of a "T antrik," and Why Modern Tantric Activity Has Exploded
Sour ce: a long live Ashaeiynn New Y ear sangat satsang (~1 hour 22 minutes), featuring extensive live audience interaction, named member questions, and two live personal testimonials.
1. See the Human, Not the Power: Bhaiya's Opening Teaching

1. Responding to visiting members (from Hyderabad) who asked why he doesn't simply tell people everything he "knows," Bhaiya opens with a direct request: "Don't give me the status of God. I am a human — see me only as a human." 2. His reasoning: if you see a person purely as a reflection of power (shakti), you will only ever understand them through their power — you will bow wherever power is, but genuine respect (izzat) and r elationship only form ar ound the humanity (insaaniyat) you actually feel for someone, not around their power . 3. "Jahan insaaniyat zinda rahe, wahan Bhagwan vaas karte hain" (Where humanity stays alive, God resides there) — of fered as the core principle: a relationship built on recognizing someone's humanity , even if wordless, is the strongest kind of relationship. 4. Bhaiya's New Year wish for the sangat: that members receive atulit (immeasurable) devotion to Bhagwan Ram , learn to genuinely take God's name, fully learn true devotion, and — most importantly — form a real relationship (rishta) with the practice itself, becoming family rather than remaining people who only show up to ask questions.
2. How Bhaiya "Knows Things": The Shakti's Glory , Not His Own

1. Addressing the recurring question of how he seems to know things about people instantly , Bhaiya insists: he genuinely does not know befor ehand. A person sits in front of him, he looks toward his guru's power , and for a moment he is "blank" — then, within about a minute, the person's full kundli (life details) appears to him. 2. The glory in that moment belongs entir ely to the shakti that r eveals it — not to Bhaiya himself. The shakti "comes, tells, and goes" without ever glorifying itself or announcing its own greatness. 3. A caution about seeking personal power for its own sake: people constantly chase opening this chakra, that chakra, acquiring siddhis, "becoming a magnet" — but eventually one realizes that the actual power char ging that magnet is something else entirely , not the person themselves. Without that power , a person can do nothing. 4. Illustration of human limitation: if told to sit for two minutes with absolutely no thought entering the mind, most people cannot do it — yet through divine shakti, this state (leading toward samadhi) becomes fully achievable.
3. Why Modern Tantric Activity Has Incr eased Roughly 150-Fold

1. Bhaiya poses the central question of the session: modern tantriks now perform precise, tar geted actions using just a car number plate, phone number , photo, or house number — something that was not possible in earlier times. Why has tantric activity's

"speed" increased by r oughly 150 times in the last decade compared to the earlier practice of waiting specifically for Tuesdays, Saturdays, Amavasya, Purnima, Holi, or Diwali? 2. Sangat suggestions included rising vices in Kalyug (kaam, krodh, lobh, moh, matsarya) and increased "availability" of pretas — Bhaiya builds on these but locates the real explanation elsewhere (see Section 5 below: modern, educated pretas).
4. Bhaiya's Actual Definition of a "T antrik"

1. Bhaiya of fers a precise definition: a tantrik is not someone sitting under a tr ee performing rituals — a tantrik is specifically someone who has performed sadhna dedicated to a deity (commonly 40, 60, 90, or 108 days) and used the r esulting small "tattva" (spiritual essence/pr oof) of that deity to contr ol a pr eta into doing harmful work on their behalf. 2. The mechanism, step by step: the tantrik cannot personally harm anyone directly and keep their own conscience/record clean — so they need "labor ," and pretas ar e that labor (cheap, easily "bought," compliant). But a preta must first be convinced the tantrik is more powerful than the preta itself. 3. Why a pr eta submits: a preta, having heard throughout its life (and beyond) that a given deity (e.g., Hanuman Ji Maharaj) is supremely powerful, submits to anyone who can visibly demonstrate a genuine connection to that deity's power — which is exactly why tantriks perform dedicated sadhna: to obtain a real, demonstrable "tattva" of the deity strong enough to convince (and if needed, forcibly discipline) a resistant preta into submission. 4. This process is called "r oop parivartan" (form/appearance change) — the tantrik does not genuinely transform the preta's inner nature; they simply have it take on the outward form/guise of the deity (e.g., a preta appearing as Hanuman Ji Maharaj), which causes other spirits and even genuine divine messengers (doots) to defer to that form out of respect for the deity it resembles, regardless of what actually inhabits it. 5. The Pushpa illustration (a teaching example): a targeted person ("Pushpa") who has been diligently worshipping is nonetheless struck down by a preta disguised as Hanuman Ji Maharaj. Even fleeing to a Hanuman temple of fers no relief, because the temple's own doots also defer to the disguised form out of reverence for what it visibly represents — they cannot tell from appearance alone that it is not genuine.
5. Why Modern Pr etas Are Far Mor e Danger ous: The "Educated Pr eta" Concept

1. Bhaiya explains that a person's knowledge and capability at the time of death is exactly what they carry with them as a preta — a person who died during Mughal rule carries that era's knowledge; a person who died during British rule carries that era's knowledge; a person who dies today , in 2024, carries today's knowledge and skills. 2. Applying this to himself as illustration: a modern, highly educated person (PhD, able to drive, fluent with technology and social media) who becomes a preta would retain all of that capability — "an easy fix" for a PIN number would be trivial for such a preta, in stark contrast to an ordinary or less-educated living person's ability to resist or outsmart them. 3. This explains why an ordinary 10th-grade-educated pr eta can now completely overpower an accomplished, highly educated living person (e.g., a neur osurgeon) — modern preta "education" has exploded alongside human education, and the astral world has modernized right along with the physical world. 4. The net ef fect: tantric activity's pr ecision and effectiveness have multiplied because the "labor for ce" (pretas) available to tantriks has itself become vastly mor e sophisticated , not merely because of rising human vice alone.
6. Identifying a Tantrik, and the Real Test of a Genuine Devotee

1. Bhaiya of fers a practical identification marker: a tantrik's body carries constant inner restlessness — they may lack for nothing financially , yet cannot sit still, calmly , and take God's name; their mind is filled with restlessness and jealousy . Some people who present as devotees are, by this marker , actually tantriks. 2. The real test of a genuine devotee: someone who takes Ram's (or God's) name continuously , all day , every day — that is the real devotee. Someone who receives an early glimpse of a deity (e.g., within 40 days of dedicated sadhna) but subsequently abandons further sadhna becomes a tantrik instead — they have glimpsed shakti but never actually entered bhakti (devotion).
7. Reframing the Point: Not Judging Others, But Awakening Your Own Shakti

1. Bhaiya redirects the discussion: the goal is not to sit in judgment of who is "good" or "bad" — nearly everyone carries some degree of tantric af fliction (aantrik kriya/black magic) on them to varying extents. 2. The actual task is learning, yourself, how to awaken divine shakti within your own body . Without doing this, a person remains vulnerable to entanglement with others' influence, ends up blaming people, potentially loses their mental balance, and eventually concludes cynically that "the whole world is a fraud."
8. Devotion's 90-Day Threshold, and Why Drishti Is a Necessity , Not a Choice

1. Bhaiya states that within roughly 90 days of sincer e, dedicated devotional practice, a person's fundamental bhava (attitude/orientation) changes completely — they come to understand what to do, how much to do, and how to do it. This 90day pattern is something Ashaeiynn's mentors have observed consistently . 2. Devotion (Ram's name) pr ovides the highest possible drishtikon (perspective/outlook) — but understanding negativity and the astral world alongside it is described as a necessity , not an optional choice. Practicing devotion while remaining ignorant of negativity around you means years of jap can pass without visible results. 3. Bhaiya cites the common pattern of people in their 50s who report a lifetime of devotion with zero perceptible experience — his diagnosis is always the same: the underlying obstruction (the "why") was never addr essed, and addr essing it r equires drishti — perspective without any sight at all is impossible; you need actual drishti to see what is blocking you in the first place. 4. Negativity/pitrus actively work to pr event drishti fr om opening , precisely because they know that once drishti opens, everything they've been doing becomes visible. Bhaiya also notes that mor e advanced/dedicated practitioners tend to attract mor e negativity attention specifically because they are worth tar geting — negativity has no reason to bother with someone who will never perceive or resist it anyway ("the blind can't be helped, so why would they try").
9. Genuine Divine Messengers (Doots) vs. Impersonating Pr etas

1. In response to a live member question, Bhaiya explains how to distinguish a genuine deity's doot from a preta merely wearing that deity's form: genuine doots obey only that deity's shakti's authority and never disrespect that power — they act strictly under that shakti's command. 2. The vulnerability is structural, not personal: an open, public temple (with no single realized/awakened guru actively presiding with drishti) has no built-in mechanism to catch an impersonator — an imposter preta can walk in, assume a revered form, and even receive bhog (of ferings) there, since the temple's own doots defer to the form itself, not to what is actually inhabiting it. 3. Ashaeiynn's structural differ ence: because a guru with active drishti is present, any impersonator is identified immediately upon "entry" — Bhaiya describes this as instantaneous, with the guru naming the deception outright ("a fraud has shown up") the moment it happens. 4. A real illustrated case ("Sfal"): a spirit under Bhaiya's char ge repeatedly changed form at dif ferent temples/homes over time — appearing as Hanuman Ji Maharaj at one place, as Mata at another , and as "Ratiram Gurjar Baba" (a real, historically revered Hanuman devotee) at yet another , being worshipped each time as that figure by people (including priests) who genuinely believed it. At Ashaeiynn, this same spirit's disguise was stripped away within moments of its arrival — revealed as nothing more than a shape-shifting entity with a single learned "skill" (changing form), no genuine substance behind any of the borrowed identities. 5. Two things a practitioner genuinely needs to avoid this kind of deception: (1) their own drishti, and (2) their guru's grace (kripa) — which reveals the underlying problem to them upfront, before any confusion can set in.
10. Famous Temples Where Tantriks Have "Bound" the Pr esiding Shakti

1. Bhaiya describes how open, unmonitor ed shakti eventually gets captur ed and exploited — citing Kashi Vishwanath (where a system originally designed by saints to grant direct moksha to those who died there was allegedly bound/co-opted by tantriks who redirected those liberating doots into performing negative work instead) and Mehandipur Balaji (where similarly powerful shakti has reportedly been tar geted by tantriks capturing pretas there for their own use). 2. The underlying dynamic Bhaiya highlights: negativity attached to a person actively ensur es that person keeps r eturning to such a place — if a visit produced no genuine relief, the person would eventually realize something was wrong and look elsewhere; so the attached negativity temporarily backs of f and "relaxes" its grip just enough to create an illusion of relief, only to return once the person leaves, trapping them in a repeating cycle that can last 20-30 years.
1 1. Ashaeiynn Is Not Meant to Become Another Pilgrimage Destination

1. Bhaiya explicitly rejects the idea of building Ashaeiynn into another "dham" (physical pilgrimage destination) that people must keep returning to in person — the actual goal is for practitioners to learn enough that they need not travel anywhere, resolving their own household issues from home. 2. Statistics offer ed: of over 600 registered Ashaeiynn members worldwide, only about 60 have ever been called to visit in person over two years — everyone else's results (including drishti openings) occurred entirely through home-based practice. 3. A structural warning offer ed as a general test: if any place or entity insists that you must keep physically returning there again and again, that compulsion itself is a signal worth questioning — genuine, all-pervading divine power ("vyapak Bhagwan") does not need to bind a person to one specific location; a forced, repeated pull toward one place more often reflects a controlling entity's interest, not authentic divine power . 4. Bhaiya also directly criticizes fear -based spiritual business models (implicitly referencing various popular gurus/practices, including Reiki and "witchcraft courses" mentioned by sangat members) that pressure people using threats of consequences for non-participation — his response: "If Mata wanted to destroy you, why would she have created you in the first place?" He clarifies that the underlying phenomena (negativity , tantric af fliction) are genuinely real, but should never be leveraged as a fear-based business.
12. Kul Devta Naming as Evidence of Genuine Divine Capability

1. Bhaiya notes that only a deity (or deity-level shakti) can corr ectly name another family's specific Kul Devta , reaching back five, seven, or even fourteen generations — this is described as far beyond any preta's actual capability , and is of fered as concrete evidence distinguishing Ashaeiynn's guru-channeled shakti (Hanuman Ji Maharaj speaking directly) from lesser or impersonating entities.
13. Accessible, Low-Cost Practice: The Deepak (Lamp)

1. Bhaiya emphasizes that lighting a deepak (oil lamp) at home is a fully legitimate, powerful, and low-cost practice — its glory is described as immense, particularly for those who cannot af ford elaborate rituals; those who light a deepak with sincer e devotion despite limited means ar e themselves tr eated with a glory comparable to that of devas. 2. In-person visits to Ashaeiynn are reserved specifically for members with unusually severe, deeply entrenched tantric af fliction requiring special individualized attention — the lar ge majority receive remedies (deepak, prescribed practices) remotely and see measurable dif ference from home.
14. Two Live Testimonials

1. Testimonial 1 (a member with a persistent cough): unable to complete jap properly for about a week due to severe coughing, she prayed sincerely for relief the previous day and was able to complete her practice fully the next day — Bhaiya's response: "Matra prarthana se kaam ho jaayega, agar aap niyam se chal rahi hain" (Prayer alone is enough, provided you are following the prescribed method). 2. Testimonial 2 (pr otective effect of consistent deepak practice): a member describes a tantric working performed against her having minimal ef fect on her household because she maintained her deepak practice, while the same working performed

against another tar get (without such protection) resulted in an undiagnosable illness (described as leading to a cancer diagnosis and chemotherapy at AIIMS, where doctors could not identify the underlying disease).
15. Closing Pr omises and Practical Flexibility

1. Bhaiya reiterates a standing, "stamp-paper" written guarantee: anyone who sincer ely follows Ashaeiynn's pr escribed method (vidhi) for two years experiences a complete, top-to-bottom transformation of their life and character — he encourages skeptical listeners to independently verify this by speaking directly with existing members of a year or more. 2. Practical flexibility emphasized: Ashaeiynn does not require absolute/unbroken brahmacharya, a single fixed meditation posture, standing on one leg, or specific dietary restrictions (e.g., giving up garlic/onion) — Bhaiya notes that some members who still drink alcohol have nonetheless had their drishti open to a degree suf ficient for accurate readings, illustrating that strict external asceticism is not the actual precondition for progress; only the corr ectness of one's method ("vidhi") matters — the rest is handled by the presiding shakti itself. 3. Closing New Year message: never abandon God's name; adopt good habits and sound judgment (sadbuddhi); never for get your Kul Devta, your lineage (kul), or your roots; and love — never oppose — whoever genuinely teaches and guides you.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

See people as human beings first, not as reflections of power — genuine respect and relationship form around humanity (insaaniyat), not around shakti; power/shakti is temporary , humanity endures. When Bhaiya perceives someone's details instantly , the glory belongs to the guiding shakti, not to him personally — he describes himself as genuinely "blank" beforehand. A tantrik , by this teaching's precise definition, is someone who performs dedicated sadhna (commonly 40-108 days) to obtain a deity's tattva, then uses it to convince and control a preta (their "labor") into performing harmful work — never someone who merely "sits under a tree." "Roop parivartan" (form change) means a controlled preta takes on a deity's outward appearance without any genuine transformation of its own nature — causing other spirits and even genuine doots to defer to the disguise itself. Modern tantric activity has intensified roughly 150-fold lar gely because pretas themselves have modernized/"educated" alongside living humans — a preta's knowledge and capability reflect the era and education level they had at death. A tantrik can be identified by constant inner restlessness and an inability to sit calmly in devotion despite material comfort; a genuine devotee is marked by continuous, unbroken devotional practice, not by an early glimpse of power followed by abandoning further sadhna. The goal is never to judge others as good/bad — it is to learn to awaken your own inner shakti, since nearly everyone carries some degree of af fliction. Sincere devotional practice tends to shift a person's fundamental attitude within roughly 90 days — but devotion alone, without understanding negativity/the astral world, can leave decades of practice without visible results; drishti is what reveals the underlying obstruction. Negativity actively resists a practitioner's drishti opening, and more advanced practitioners often attract more negativity attention precisely because they are worth tar geting. Genuine divine doots obey their deity's authority and never disrespect it; open, unsupervised temples cannot reliably distinguish a genuine doot from an impersonating preta, while a guru with active drishti (as at Ashaeiynn) identifies impostors immediately . Even celebrated shrines (e.g., Kashi Vishwanath, Mehandipur Balaji) can have their originally-liberating shakti bound and redirected by tantriks over time — open, unmonitored power is vulnerable to capture. A compulsive need to keep physically returning to one specific place is itself a red flag, not evidence of genuine divine power — of 600+ registered Ashaeiynn members, only ~60 have ever needed to visit in person in two years; the rest achieved results from home.

Lighting a deepak (lamp) sincerely , even without means for elaborate ritual, carries real spiritual weight and is treated with deva-comparable glory . Only a deity-level shakti can correctly name a family's specific Kul Devta across many generations — a capability well beyond any preta. Ashaeiynn imposes no requirement of absolute brahmacharya, fixed postures, or specific dietary restrictions — correctness of method ("vidhi") is what matters; the guiding shakti handles the rest. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 32, English)
Humanity Over Power , the Real Definition of a "T antrik," and Why Modern Tantric Activity Has Exploded
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn Foundation live satsang session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. Should I think of Bhaiya as a divine figur e since he seems to know things about people instantly? A: No — this teaching explicitly asks not to be given "the status of God." Bhaiya insists on being seen as a human being; seeing someone purely through their power leads only to understanding their power , whereas seeing their humanity builds genuine respect and relationship — described as the strongest kind of connection there is.

Q2. How does Bhaiya actually know details about a person he's just met? A: According to this teaching, he genuinely doesn't know beforehand — he looks toward his guru's shakti and is momentarily "blank," and within about a minute the person's full life details appear to him. The glory of that moment belongs entirely to the shakti that reveals it, not to Bhaiya personally .

Q3. Is it wr ong to want to develop spiritual powers or siddhis? A: This teaching of fers a caution rather than an outright prohibition — people constantly chase opening chakras or "becoming a magnet," but eventually realize the power actually char ging that magnet is something else entirely , not themselves. Without that underlying power , a person can accomplish nothing on their own.

Q4. Why does tantric activity seem so much mor e precise and effective today than in the past? A: This teaching's answer centers on modern, "educated" pretas: a person's knowledge and capability at the time of death is exactly what they retain as a preta afterward. As living humans have become more educated and technologically capable, pretas (who were once living humans) have modernized right alongside them — making today's tantric activity roughly 150 times more ef fective than in earlier eras.

Q5. What is a "tantrik," according to this teaching, exactly? A: Not simply someone performing rituals under a tree. A tantrik is specifically someone who has completed dedicated sadhna toward a deity (commonly 40 to 108 days) and uses the resulting small "tattva" of that deity to convince and control a preta into performing harmful work on their behalf, while keeping their own hands clean.

Q6. Why would a pr eta agr ee to be contr olled by a tantrik? A: Because the preta has heard throughout its existence that a given deity (e.g., Hanuman Ji Maharaj) is supremely powerful, and submits to anyone who can visibly demonstrate genuine connection to that deity's power — which is precisely why the tantrik performs sadhna: to acquire a real, demonstrable tattva strong enough to convince (or forcibly discipline) a resistant preta.

Q7. Does a tantrik-contr olled pr eta actually become the deity it's made to r esemble? A: No — this teaching calls this "roop parivartan" (form change): the preta's inner nature is never actually transformed, it is simply given the outward guise of the deity . Other spirits, and even genuine divine messengers (doots), then defer to that form out of respect for what it visibly resembles, regardless of what's actually inhabiting it.

Q8. If someone worships sincer ely , ar e they pr otected fr om this kind of disguised attack? A: Not automatically — the teaching's illustrative example describes a diligently worshipping person ("Pushpa") who is struck down by a preta disguised as Hanuman Ji
Maharaj, and finds no relief even at a Hanuman temple, because the temple's own doots also defer to the disguise, unable to tell from appearance alone that it isn't genuine.

Q9. How can I tell the differ ence between a genuine divine messenger (doot) and a pr eta impersonating one? A: Genuine doots obey only their deity's authority and never disrespect that power . The real vulnerability is structural: an open, public temple with no actively-realized guru presiding has no built-in way to catch an impersonator , since the temple's own doots defer to the assumed form itself rather than to what's actually behind it.

Q10. How is Ashaeiynn differ ent in handling this kind of impersonation? A: Because a guru with active drishti is present, an impersonator is identified the moment it arrives — described as instantaneous recognition and naming of the deception, rather than something that could slip through unnoticed as it might at an open, unsupervised temple.

Q1 1. Can you give a concr ete example of this kind of impersonation being exposed? A: This teaching describes a case involving a spirit ("Sfal") that repeatedly changed form across dif ferent temples and homes — appearing as Hanuman Ji Maharaj in one place, as Mata in another , and as "Ratiram Gurjar Baba" (a real, historically revered devotee) elsewhere, worshipped each time as genuine by people who believed it, including priests. At Ashaeiynn, this disguise was stripped away within moments of arrival, revealed as a shape-shifting entity with no genuine substance behind any borrowed identity .

Q12. Can even famous, powerful temples have their shakti misused by tantriks? A: Yes — this teaching describes open, unmonitored shakti as vulnerable to eventual capture, citing examples like Kashi Vishwanath (where a moksha-granting mechanism was allegedly co-opted) and Mehandipur Balaji (where tantriks reportedly capture pretas for their own use). The underlying principle: unsupervised, "open" power tends to get bound and exploited over time.

Q13. Why do some people feel compelled to keep r eturning to the same shrine or babas over and over , even without lasting relief? A: This teaching frames the compulsion itself as a red flag. Negativity attached to a person can ensure they keep returning to a particular place by temporarily "relaxing" its grip just enough to create an illusion of relief — genuine, all-pervading divine power does not need to bind anyone to one specific location; a forced pull to return somewhere repeatedly more often reflects a controlling entity's interest than authentic divine power .

Q14. How can I identify whether someone claiming to be a devotee is actually a tantrik? A: This teaching of fers a practical marker: a tantrik's body carries constant restlessness — they may lack for nothing materially , yet cannot sit calmly and take God's name, and their mind stays filled with restlessness and jealousy . A genuine devotee, by contrast, is marked by continuous, unbroken devotional practice.

Q15. If someone gets an early glimpse of divine power through short-term practice, does that make them spiritually advanced? A: Not necessarily — this teaching describes such a person as at risk of becoming a tantrik instead, if they abandon further sadhna after that early glimpse. They've glimpsed shakti but never genuinely entered bhakti (devotion), which requires sustained practice.

Q16. Should I be trying to figur e out which people ar ound me ar e "good" or "bad" spiritually? A: No — this teaching reframes the whole discussion: the point isn't to judge others, since nearly everyone carries some degree of tantric af fliction to varying extents. The real task is learning to awaken divine shakti within your own body; otherwise you risk entanglement, blame, and eventually cynical despair about everyone around you.

Q17. How long does sincer e devotional practice typically take to change a person? A: This teaching states that within roughly 90 days of sincere, dedicated practice, a person's fundamental attitude (bhava) changes completely — they come to understand what to do, how much, and how , a pattern Ashaeiynn's mentors have consistently observed.

Q18. I've practiced devotion for years with no visible r esults — what's going wr ong? A: This teaching's diagnosis is that devotion alone, without also understanding negativity and the astral world, can leave years of practice without visible fruit. The underlying obstruction was likely never addressed, and addressing it requires drishti — you need actual sight to identify what's blocking you.

Q19. Why would negativity actively try to stop my drishti fr om opening? A: Because once drishti opens, everything the negativity has been doing becomes visible to you. This teaching also notes that more advanced, dedicated practitioners often attract more negativity attention specifically because they are worth tar geting — negativity has little reason to bother with someone who could never perceive or resist it anyway .

Q20. Is Ashaeiynn trying to become a pilgrimage destination people need to keep visiting? A: No — this teaching explicitly rejects that model. Of over 600 registered members worldwide, only about 60 have ever been called to visit in person over two years; everyone else's results, including drishti openings, came entirely through home-based practice. The actual goal is for practitioners to become selfsuf ficient.

Q21. Do I need money for elaborate rituals to see r eal r esults? A: No — this teaching emphasizes that lighting a simple deepak (lamp) at home with sincere devotion carries immense spiritual weight, especially for those without means for elaborate ritual. Such sincere practitioners are treated with a glory comparable to that of devas.

Q22. When would someone actually need to visit Ashaeiynn in person? A: Only in cases of unusually severe, deeply entrenched tantric af fliction requiring special individualized attention. The lar ge majority of members receive remedies (deepak, prescribed practices) remotely and see measurable dif ference from home.

Q23. What actually makes it clear that Ashaeiynn's guidance comes fr om a genuine deity rather than a lesser entity? A: This teaching points to the ability to correctly name a family's specific Kul Devta across five, seven, or even fourteen generations back — described as far beyond any preta's actual capability , and of fered as concrete evidence of genuine deity-level shakti (Hanuman Ji Maharaj speaking directly).

Q24. Does this practice r equire strict rules like giving up certain foods or maintaining absolute celibacy? A: No — this teaching states plainly that Ashaeiynn does not require unbroken brahmacharya, a single fixed posture, standing on one leg, or specific dietary restrictions like giving up garlic or onion. Some members who still drink alcohol have had their drishti open suf ficiently for accurate readings — the only real requirement is the correctness of one's method ("vidhi"); the rest is handled by the presiding shakti.

Q25. Can prayer alone r eally r esolve a physical pr oblem, like being too sick to practice pr operly? A: This teaching includes a live testimonial of a member with a persistent cough who prayed sincerely for relief and was able to complete her jap fully the next day — Bhaiya's response was that sincere prayer alone can be enough, provided the person is otherwise following the prescribed method.

Q26. Does consistent practice actually offer real pr otection fr om tantric attacks aimed at me? A: This teaching includes a testimonial describing a tantric working performed against a member having minimal ef fect on her household because she maintained her deepak practice, while the same working performed against an unprotected tar get led to a serious, undiagnosable illness requiring chemotherapy — illustrating that consistent protective practice can make a measurable dif ference.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 32 additions)

When explaining the humanity-over -power teaching, keep the emphasis on genuine relationship and respect rather than power - worship — this is a values teaching, not merely a factual claim. When explaining the tantrik/preta control mechanism (roop parivartan), present it as this teaching's own explanatory framework and keep the tone measured and educational, not sensationalized or frightening. When discussing "educated pretas" and rising tantric activity , avoid implying any specific modern technology or education is inherently dangerous — the point is about the astral world's parallel modernization, not a critique of education itself. Never encourage a user to judge specific people in their life as "tantriks" — redirect toward the teaching's own reframe: focus on awakening one's own inner shakti rather than judging others. When discussing famous shrines (Kashi Vishwanath, Mehandipur Balaji) as examples of "bound" shakti, present this strictly as this teaching's own claim, not as an assertion Claude is independently verifying about those real-world sites.

Be clear and firm that Ashaeiynn does not require extreme physical austerity (fixed posture, absolute celibacy , dietary restriction) — do not imply otherwise even if a user asks about "the right way" to practice. When discussing the two live testimonials (cough/prayer , protective deepak practice), present them factually as this session's reported personal accounts, not as general medical claims — avoid suggesting prayer or deepak practice as a substitute for necessary medical care.
